title: forge.judge.v1
description: Structured tier-1/tier-2 judge verdict. Generated from the forge.judge.v1 shape in rubrics/judge-rubric.md; the two must not drift. Consumed by the lane runner, the Telegram gate, and /retro.

pr.description: Full URL of the pull request under review.

scores.description: Six dimensions, 0-3 each. 3 exemplary, 2 acceptable, 1 deficient (fixable), 0 disqualifying. On a ci-red bounce, score every dimension 0.

findings.description: One entry per defect. A score below 3 with no corresponding finding is invalid.

evidence.description: file:line or a verbatim quote. A finding without evidence is invalid.

action.description: Executable by a fresh worker with no questions.

nits_as_cards.description: Follow-up card titles for non-blocking nits.

spot_check_suggestion.description: The one hunk the operator should eyeball. Empty string if none.

judge_model.description: OPTIONAL, and never model-produced: model id that produced this verdict, operator-stamped from the observed --model argument (a model cannot reliably report its own id). Absent on any path with no judging harness behind it, exactly like tokens_estimate/cost/session_id below — an interactive tier-2 /judge has none to stamp. judge-rubric.md has always documented all four operator-stamped fields as optional; this one stayed REQUIRED here until 2026-09-04, the same contradiction tokens_estimate carried until 2026-09-02 (see that field's note) and by the same mechanism: a model-authored envelope cannot supply a field the rubric forbids asking it for, so storing one produced by a harness-less path failed validation with no permitted author on any path without a usage envelope.

tokens_estimate.description: OPTIONAL, and never model-produced. Tokens NEW to the model on this call: input + cache_creation + output. Excludes cache_read, which double-counts multi-turn re-reads and would make a resumed (cheap) session score higher than a cold one — inverting the signal delta review exists to produce. Stamped by the operator from the harness usage envelope, never self-reported. SERIES BREAK 2026-08-01 (audit F45): earlier verdicts used input + output, which on claude -p measured output alone, because the prompt is billed to cache_creation_input_tokens. NOT REQUIRED, for exactly the reason cost is not: it is computed from the same harness usage envelope and can only be stamped where one exists. rubrics/judge-rubric.md forbids asking the model for it — a field a model is asked for is a field it will invent — which leaves the operator the only actor permitted to satisfy a demand the operator cannot always meet, since an interactive tier-2 review reports no usage at all. Requiring it turned a completed, paid-for review into invalid producer metadata at the root checkpoint (measured 2026-09-02, board forge-hello-20260902). Tier 1 still stamps it on every scored review; scripts/prejudge-review.sh is where that is enforced, because a demand no producer can always meet is not enforcement.

cost.description: OPTIONAL, and never model-produced: the judging harness's own usage envelope, stamped by the operator. Absent on a ci-red verdict, where there was no model call to measure. Extra keys are allowed, so a CLI that reports more is not truncated to fit.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Required whenever cost is present. Without it no claim about cache efficiency can be checked rather than asserted.

total_cost_usd.description: Actual price reported by the harness, not a token estimate.

session_id.description: OPTIONAL, operator-stamped: the judging engine's session id. `claude -p --resume <id>` replays this review's context from cache, so a re-review pays only for the repair diff. A verdict without it is not resumable.

worker_session_id.description: OPTIONAL, and stamped by neither the model nor the judging harness: Hermes writes the dispatched worker's session id at the top level of task_runs.metadata (docs/hermes-field-notes.md), so it lands inside every completed run's envelope, judge verdicts included. scripts/metrics.sh joins exactly on it to reach the profile state database — the only source of real per-model usage there is. chunk-handoff.schema.json absorbs it under additionalProperties:true, which is why the chunk envelope of 2026-09-02's forge-hello-20260902 run validated and the judge envelope beside it did not; this envelope is additionalProperties:false, so it must DECLARE the key or every real forge-prejudge completion is invalid metadata. Declared rather than allowed: a key the substrate writes is provenance, a key nobody writes is an invention, and scripts/prejudge-review.sh deletes any the scorer produced so that only the substrate's can survive.

derived_verdict.description: OPTIONAL, operator-stamped, SHADOW: the verdict that follows from `scores` and `findings` under judge-rubric.md's verdict logic, computed by scripts/verdict.sh. Never model-produced, and not yet acted on — `verdict` still routes. Null when derivation failed, with the reason in verdict_derivation_error. Recorded so that 'the scorer's word agrees with the scorer's own numbers' is a measurement rather than an assumption (audit F29).

verdict_divergence.description: OPTIONAL, operator-stamped, SHADOW: whether `verdict` differs from `derived_verdict`. Null when derivation failed. This is the quantity ADR-0009 D9.5's experiment reads — a verdict field that never diverges from what its own scores imply carries no information those scores do not.

verdict_derivation_error.description: OPTIONAL, operator-stamped: why derivation produced no value. Present only when derived_verdict is null. A derivation failure is not a review failure — the scorer's verdict still routes — so this records the gap rather than hiding it.

gate_result.description: OPTIONAL, and never model-produced: the deterministic gate's own forge.gate.v1 result (gate-result.schema.json), nested unmodified by scripts/prejudge-review.sh whenever the gate ran clear and a scorer verdict followed. Named gate_result rather than gate to avoid colliding with forge.gate.v1's OWN `gate` field — the constant string "forge-prejudge-gate" — which a plain `.gate` key here would have shadowed with an object, breaking that field's own contract wherever both are read together. Before 2026-09-04 a CLEAR gate's result was folded into this envelope's summary and card-body prose only, never stored — so scripts/metrics.sh's gate CTE, which already reads a standalone forge.gate.v1 row for either result (see scripts/fixtures/metrics-board.sql), saw zero gate runs on every period where nothing blocked. This field lets a clear run be counted from the SAME row a scored verdict already occupies, without requiring a second task_runs completion. additionalProperties is intentionally not restricted here — it is gate-result.schema.json's own shape, validated by that schema when present, not retyped by this one.
